description: Our team focuses on exploring terrestrial analog environments by comparing Earth's geological, topographical, and environmental characteristics with those of the Moon and Mars. We aim to utilize open-source NASA datasets, satellite imagery, and scientific analysis to identify and characterize potential locations for testing future planetary exploration technologies and supporting mission planning.
summary: Our project is an interactive website designed to explore potential locations on Earth that share environmental and geological characteristics with the Moon and Mars. Using an interactive map, users can explore five candidate locations: Ladakh, Rann of Kutch, Atacama Desert, Spiti Valley, and Icelandic volcanic terrain. The website provides information about the environmental similarities of each location and explains their possible relevance to future lunar and Martian exploration. It also highlights the limitations of these comparisons. Our goal is to demonstrate how Earth-based analogue environments can help us understand the challenges of establishing future human bases beyond Earth.
details:
Project VASTIANS – TERRAFORM is an interactive web-based platform developed to explore potential Earth locations that resemble environmental conditions found on the Moon and Mars.

The website uses an interactive map powered by Leaflet and OpenStreetMap to display five candidate locations: Ladakh, Rann of Kutch, Atacama Desert, Spiti Valley, and Icelandic volcanic terrain.

Users can select Moon or Mars filters to explore locations and understand their environmental similarities. Each location includes a brief explanation of its characteristics, possible relevance to space exploration, and limitations.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It is hosted using GitHub Pages, making it accessible through a web browser.

Our project demonstrates how Earth-based analogue environments can support the study of challenges associated with future human exploration and settlement on the Moon and Mars. The current comparisons are qualitative and require further scientific validation using relevant Earth, lunar, and Martian datasets.
dataRefs: Our project is inspired by the goal of using Earth-based analogue environments to support future lunar and Martian exploration. We identified relevant NASA datasets, including lunar topography data from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and Mars elevation data from the Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA), as potential sources for future scientific validation. However, these datasets have not yet been downloaded or quantitatively processed in the current version. Our present comparisons are qualitative.
projectRefs: The project uses OpenStreetMap for interactive map visualization and Leaflet JavaScript library for displaying geographical locations. We also used general geographical and environmental information about Ladakh, Rann of Kutch, Atacama Desert, Spiti Valley, and Icelandic volcanic terrain to develop our qualitative comparisons.
